messages:
Jorge: heads-up — ran a comparison of packing strategies with mixed-precision kernels (FP8/INT8/4-bit) + continuous batching on the latency branch. results are... weird.
Eva: ping, can you paste numbers? also which model/seq-len? :eyes: 
Jorge: mt-large, seq=128 and seq=2048, batch RSVP load from prod trace. three configs: (A) baseline fp16 kernels + dynamic batcher, (B) int8/4-bit packing with per-batch calibration, (C) fp8 kernels + packing. KV-cache enabled for all.
Sam: is this the new packer that aligns to 64B lanes? last PR changed slab layout.
Jorge: yes — packer v2 (align 64). slab allocator returned slightly different offsets -> extra memcpy when kv cache hit path did rebase.
Rita: tl;dr numbers?
Jorge: seq128 throughput (tokens/sec): A=1.0x, B=0.82x, C=0.95x relative to A. mean p50 latency: A=38ms, B=46ms, C=41ms. seq2048 throughput: A=1.0x, B=1.12x, C=1.34x. p50: A=520ms, B=460ms, C=380ms.
Eva: so INT8/4-bit costs us at short seqs due to overhead, but wins at long seq. FP8 is best at long seqs. makes sense.
Jorge: yes. profiling shows kernel time scaling and launch/pack overhead tradeoff. for seq128, dequant + re-quant + packer compute ~28% overhead in B. trace:
```
[perf] timeline: launch(2.1ms) -> pack(1.9ms) -> dequant(3.4ms) -> kernel(26ms) -> re-quant(2.2ms)
```
Sam: interesting — pack + dequant exceed kernel savings for short sequences.
Rita: what about padding waste with continuous batching? did packer increase padding due to shape constraints?
Jorge: yes, observed effective padding ratio jump from 12%->29% when enabling packer v2 + continuous-batcher. reason: packer forces shapes to multiples of 8 lanes for INT4 kernels and 16 for FP8; continuous batcher prefers grouping by arrival window not exact length -> more padding.
Eva: can we change batcher heuristic to avoid grouping small with large? maybe windowed bucketing by length_mod rather than raw length.
Sam: another angle: allow packer to emit 'sparse' layout for short sequences (no pad) at cost of extra kernel branch.
Jorge: tried a hybrid: if padding > 20% then fallback to fp16 kernel for that batch. fallback reduced latency p50 by ~9% for seq128, but killed throughput for long seq workloads (because it broke kernel selection inertia and cold-started fp16 paths).
perf-bot: perf-bot report attached (summary): packer_v2+continuous: p50 up 8ms @ seq128, p50 down 120ms @ seq2048, cpu memcpy up 18%
Rita: KV-cache behavior? you mentioned memcpy earlier.
Jorge: yes — slab rebase on cache hit (due to align change) caused extra host<->device staging for ~6% of requests. that explains some of the short-tail latencies. patched allocator to keep sticky device pointers for hot slabs — preliminary reduced extra memcpy to 0.6%.
Eva: calibration effects? per-batch calibration adds overhead right?
Jorge: per-batch EMA scale calibration we tried adds ~0.9ms/batch (seq128) and ~6ms/batch (seq2048) but improves generation quality (BLEU/ROUGE type evals) for int4 in long runs. also calibration interacts with caching: cached kv uses previous scales, sometimes mismatch forces re-calculation -> rare but visible.
Sam: any accuracy regressions when using fp8 vs int8? we need regression test set.
Jorge: fp8 had ~0.3% quality delta vs fp16 on our prompt set; int4 ~2.1% delta without repeated calibration, 0.9% with per-batch calibration. tradeoffs obvious.
Rita: actionable next steps?
Jorge: propose:
- revert packer v2 alignment for small slabs (or add short-seq path)
- add batcher bucketing by length_mod (mod 8/16) to reduce padding mixing
- sticky-device pointers for allocator (ship patch)
- optional lightweight cached-scale check to avoid full re-calibration on cached KV hits
- add perf unit that simulates 1M continuous batches with prod trace to catch regressions
Sam: +1 to all. can we also emit exp metrics per-token: pack-overhead, kv-memcpy-rate in console?
Eva: yes, add to Optimize dashboard: packing_overhead_ms, padding_ratio, kv_rebase_pct.
Infra-bot: deploy candidate: allocator-sticky + batcher-bucket landed to canary (infra/canary). CI perf tests scheduled.
Rita: let's monitor canary for 48h then decide. thanks for the deep dive, Jorge.
Jorge: will follow up with the full perf dump and the small repro kernel to try locally. attaching link to mini-trace: https://artifacts.redwood/trace/1798765432/pack-sample
Sam: nice. if someone wants to reproduce quickly:
```
# run local repro
python tools/repro/run_pack_test.py --model mt-large --seqs 128,2048 --pack-mode v2 --kv
```
Eva: tagging @eng-runtime for visibility. :shipit:
